## Report Header

Filing institution: Cortex Bank and Trust
Internal case reference: FIU-2024-1721
Report filed: September 19, 2024
Suspected activity: structuring / CTR avoidance
Risk tier: high
Subjects of this report:
  Elowen Oyelaran (individual), account 13-66819-1
Review period: March 1, 2024 through July 30, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $502,959.25

## Activity Overview

This review was initiated following an automated monitoring alert generated on July 30, 2024, concerning activity in account 13-66819-1, held in the name of Elowen Oyelaran. The alert identified patterns of cash deposits that appeared designed to circumvent Currency Transaction Report requirements. The review period for this analysis spans from March 1, 2024, through July 30, 2024. During this timeframe, the aggregate cash volume deposited into the account totaled $502,959.25. The activity under review primarily consists of physical cash deposits made at various Cortex Bank and Trust branch locations, followed by outbound wire transfers. The suspected typology is structuring, also known as CTR avoidance, characterized by a series of cash transactions conducted in amounts just below the $10,000 regulatory reporting threshold.

The account in question, 13-66819-1, is a personal checking account. Customer profile information indicates the primary source of wealth is salary, though the volume of cash moving through the account during the review period appears inconsistent with typical salaried income. The activity exhibits several characteristics commonly associated with attempts to evade reporting requirements. The deposits observed were frequently clustered in amounts between $3,495.21 and $1,445.00. For instance, on March 8, 2024, a deposit of $9,080.01 was recorded. This pattern continued with subsequent deposits, including $8,368.99 on March 29, 2024, and $9,095.70 on April 26, 2024. These amounts are notably close to the $10,000 threshold, suggesting a deliberate effort to keep individual transactions below the reporting requirement.

In addition to the transaction amounts, the behavior of the transactor at the branch level raised concerns. A review of branch referral logs associated with the alert indicated that on several occasions during the review period, the transactor asked branch staff specific questions regarding the thresholds for cash reporting. Such inquiries, while not definitively indicative of illicit intent, are often considered a red flag when coupled with transaction patterns that suggest structuring. Furthermore, the deposits were not confined to a single branch location. The activity records demonstrate instances of branch rotation, where deposits were made at different Cortex Bank and Trust branches on the same business day or within a short time frame, further supporting the suspicion of deliberate CTR avoidance.

The disposition of the funds following the cash deposits also forms a critical component of the suspicious activity profile. The analysis revealed that the cash deposits were frequently followed by outbound transfers. In several instances, the funds were moved out of the account via wire transfer shortly after the cash was deposited, often in amounts that closely mirrored the aggregate of the recent cash deposits. The largest single outbound transfer during the review period was for $131,942.91. This rapid movement of funds, particularly when the outbound transfers align with the incoming cash volume, suggests that the account is being used as a conduit for the funds rather than for typical personal banking purposes. The counterparties for these outbound transfers included Hearthstone Distribution LLC, Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd., and Bramblewood Trading Partners LP. The relationship between Elowen Oyelaran and these entities is unclear based on the account profile, and the volume and velocity of the funds transferred appear inconsistent with the stated purpose of the personal checking account. The combination of sub-threshold cash deposits, branch rotation, inquiries about reporting thresholds, and the subsequent rapid transfer of funds to seemingly unrelated entities warrants further investigation to determine the nature and purpose of this activity.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

Elowen Oyelaran established a relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust on February 12, 2021, opening a personal checking account (13-66819-1). At onboarding, the customer indicated she was a self-employed business consultant operating a sole proprietorship. The expected activity profile recorded during the initial risk assessment anticipated a moderate volume of domestic wire transfers and ACH payments, primarily from consulting clients, with estimated monthly inflows of a low five-figure sum. Cash activity was expected to be nominal, with occasional small withdrawals for personal expenses. The account was assigned a moderate risk rating, reflecting the self-employed status and the anticipated volume of electronic funds transfers. The customer’s profile was last updated in November 2023, at which time the customer confirmed the ongoing nature of her consulting business and the expected activity profile remained unchanged. The customer does not hold any credit products or other deposit accounts with Cortex Bank and Trust.

A review of the account’s historical activity prior to the current review period indicated transactional behavior generally aligned with the expected profile. Inflows consisted primarily of ACH credits and domestic wire transfers from various commercial entities, while outflows were characterized by typical personal expenditures, including debit card point-of-sale transactions, ACH debits for utility payments, and occasional small cash withdrawals. Cash deposits were infrequent and immaterial in value. The account did not generate any automated alerts or manual referrals for suspicious activity prior to the events detailed in this report. The relationship manager noted no unusual interactions or concerns during routine periodic reviews.

The transactional activity observed during the review period represented a significant departure from both the historical baseline and the expected activity profile recorded at onboarding. The primary deviation was the sudden and substantial influx of cash deposits into the personal checking account. The aggregate cash volume deposited during the review period was $502,959.25, a figure that starkly contrasts with the nominal cash activity anticipated for a self-employed business consultant. This volume of cash is not consistent with the declared occupation, as consulting services are typically remunerated via electronic funds transfers or checks, rather than large sums of physical currency. The customer was unable to substantiate a legitimate business purpose for this volume of cash when queried by branch staff during routine interactions.

Furthermore, the nature of the outflows shifted significantly during the review period. While the historical activity demonstrated a pattern of routine personal expenditures, the current review period saw a marked increase in large outbound transfers. The most notable of these was a single outbound transfer totaling $131,942.91, which was directed to Hearthstone Distribution LLC. This transfer, along with other substantial outbound payments to Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. and Bramblewood Trading Partners LP, suggests the account may be utilized for commercial purposes rather than the personal use for which it was established. The use of a personal account to facilitate what appears to be commercial activity, particularly involving significant cash deposits and large outbound transfers to corporate entities, is a material deviation from the customer’s stated profile.

The counterparties receiving the outbound funds—Hearthstone Distribution LLC, Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd., and Bramblewood Trading Partners LP—do not appear to have an obvious connection to the customer’s declared occupation as a business consultant. The nature of these entities, as suggested by their names, implies involvement in distribution, produce, and trading, sectors that typically operate with distinct financial profiles and supply chains. The routing of significant funds, originating from unexplained cash deposits, to these specific entities raises questions regarding the economic purpose of the transactions and the true nature of the customer’s business activities. The reviewing analyst noted that the combination of the unexpected cash volume, the shift in outflow patterns, and the involvement of these specific counterparties indicates a fundamental change in how the account is being utilized, contradicting the information provided by the customer at onboarding and during subsequent reviews.

## Account Profile and Baseline Activity

The subject of this review, Elowen Oyelaran, maintains an individual checking account with Cortex Bank and Trust, designated as account 13-66819-1. The account was established in early 2021, and Elowen Oyelaran is the sole listed owner. The relationship manager profile indicates Elowen Oyelaran is self-employed as a consultant in the food service logistics sector. Initial account funding was unremarkable, consisting of a low four-figure electronic transfer from another domestic financial institution.

Historical activity in the account prior to the review period commencing March 1, 2024, established a predictable baseline. Monthly credit volume averaged a low five-figure amount, primarily comprised of two or three incoming automated clearing house credits per month. These credits were typically originated by domestic business entities and appeared commensurate with Elowen Oyelaran's stated occupation. Cash deposits were infrequent and of low value, generally occurring less than once per quarter and never exceeding a low four-figure sum.

Debit activity during the historical period was similarly predictable. Monthly debit volume generally matched credit volume, resulting in a stable average monthly balance. Debits primarily consisted of point-of-sale transactions, recurring automated clearing house payments for consumer utilities, and occasional small-value funds transfers to other domestic financial institutions. The account profile and transaction history prior to March 2024 were consistent with the expected activity for an individual consumer account and presented a low risk profile.

The transaction monitoring system maintained statistical baselines for the account based on this historical activity. The expected monthly cash deposit volume was set at a low four-figure threshold, and the expected frequency of cash deposits was less than one per month. The anticipated monthly aggregate credit volume was established in the low five-figure range. The monitoring system also established baselines for the size and frequency of outgoing funds transfers, which were historically small and infrequent.

Activity within account 13-66819-1 deviated significantly from these established baselines beginning in early March 2024. The volume and frequency of cash deposits increased dramatically, rendering the historical baseline obsolete. The aggregate cash volume deposited during the review period was $502,959.25. This volume represents a substantial departure from the expected activity for this account and is fundamentally inconsistent with Elowen Oyelaran's stated occupation and historical transaction profile. The frequency of cash deposits also increased markedly, with multiple deposits often occurring within a single week.

The nature of the cash deposits also changed during the review period. Historically, cash deposits were irregular in amount and infrequent. During the review period, the cash deposits were concentrated in amounts clustered between $3,495.21 and $1,445.00. These deposits were consistently placed below the $10,000 regulatory threshold for currency transaction reporting. The timing and amounts of these deposits, viewed in aggregate, suggest a pattern of activity designed to avoid the reporting requirements associated with large cash transactions.

The debit activity within the account also experienced a corresponding shift. The increased cash deposit volume was typically followed by outgoing funds transfers. These transfers were often executed shortly after the cash deposits cleared. The outgoing funds transfers were frequently directed to Hearthstone Distribution LLC, Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd., and Bramblewood Trading Partners LP. The volume of these transfers significantly exceeded the historical baseline for outgoing funds transfers. The largest single outbound transfer that followed the deposits was $131,942.91.

The shift in account activity from infrequent, low-value electronic credits to frequent, high-value cash deposits followed by large outgoing funds transfers represents a fundamental change in the account profile. The activity observed during the review period is not consistent with the historical baseline established for Elowen Oyelaran's account. The volume of cash introduced into the account, coupled with the subsequent outgoing funds transfers, requires further analysis to determine the nature and purpose of the transactions.

## Transaction Analysis

During the review period from March 1, 2024 through July 30, 2024, the account held by Elowen Oyelaran (13-66819-1) exhibited a pattern of cash deposits that appeared designed to circumvent the $10,000 regulatory reporting threshold. The aggregate cash volume deposited during this period reached $502,959.25. The reviewing analyst noted that these deposits were frequently clustered in amounts between $3,495.21 and $1,445.00. The timing and sequencing of these transactions, particularly the execution of multiple deposits on the same day across different branch locations, strongly indicated an intent to evade currency transaction reporting requirements.

The structural features of this activity were evident early in the review period. On March 1, 2024, a deposit of $9,080.01 was recorded at a branch location in the morning. Later that same day, a second deposit of $8,368.99 was executed at a different branch location. The total cash deposited on this date exceeded the $10,000 reporting threshold, yet neither individual transaction triggered a report. This branch rotation strategy, executed within a single business day, is a classic indicator of structuring.

A similar pattern emerged on March 15, 2024, when a deposit of $9,095.70 was recorded. The reviewing analyst identified that these sub-threshold deposits were not isolated incidents but part of a sustained strategy. The velocity of these transactions was notable, with multiple deposits often occurring within a single week. The consistent clustering of deposit amounts just below the reporting threshold further substantiated the suspicion of deliberate avoidance.

The relationship between the incoming cash deposits and subsequent outbound activity was also analyzed. The reviewing analyst observed that the cash deposits were frequently followed by outbound transfers. The largest single outbound transfer during the review period was $131,942.91. This transfer, while substantial, did not appear to correspond directly to the accumulated cash deposits, suggesting a commingling of funds or a more complex disbursement strategy. However, the reviewing analyst did note instances where cash deposits were followed in close proximity by outbound transfers of similar amounts, indicating a potential attempt to quickly move the deposited funds out of the account.

The sequencing of these transactions relative to business hours and reporting cutoffs provided additional context. While the specific times of the deposits varied, the consistent use of multiple branches on the same day suggested a calculated effort to avoid detection by branch staff. On March 29, 2024, the reviewing analyst noted a deposit that occurred late in the business day, shortly before the branch closing time. While this timing alone is not definitive, when viewed in conjunction with the broader pattern of activity, it raised concerns about an attempt to minimize scrutiny.

Further analysis of the transaction data revealed ongoing sub-threshold cash deposit activity throughout April and May. On April 2, 2024, and again on April 11, 2024, deposits were recorded that aligned with the previously observed clustering pattern. The reviewing analyst also noted activity on April 26, 2024, and May 14, 2024, which continued the trend of frequent, sub-threshold cash deposits. The consistency of this activity over several months suggested a deliberate and sustained effort to manage the flow of cash into the account in a manner that avoided regulatory reporting.

The reviewing analyst noted that during a transaction on May 28, 2024, the customer engaged branch staff in a conversation regarding reporting thresholds. While the specific details of this interaction are documented elsewhere, the inquiry itself, in the context of the observed transaction pattern, provided further indication of the customer's awareness of and potential intent to evade regulatory requirements. The combination of branch rotation, clustered sub-threshold deposit amounts, and customer inquiries regarding reporting thresholds strongly supported the assessment that the transaction pattern was suspicious rather than merely unusual. The velocity and volume of the cash deposits, coupled with the subsequent outbound transfers, indicated a sophisticated understanding of banking operations and a deliberate attempt to conceal the true nature and origin of the funds.

## Counterparty and Beneficiary Analysis

A review of the outgoing wire transfers from Elowen Oyelaran's account (13-66819-1) during the review period was conducted to determine the beneficiaries and the economic purpose of the transactions. The analysis indicated that the funds deposited in cash, totaling the aggregate amount of $502,959.25, were subsequently transferred to a small network of entities. The primary beneficiaries identified were Hearthstone Distribution LLC, Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd., and Bramblewood Trading Partners LP. The outbound activity was characterized by rapid movement of funds following the cash deposits, often occurring on the same or the subsequent business day.

Hearthstone Distribution LLC received a significant portion of the outgoing funds. Internal records indicate that Elowen Oyelaran previously stated this entity was a primary supplier of agricultural goods. A review of state corporate registry filings confirmed that Hearthstone Distribution LLC is an active limited liability company formed two years prior to the review period. However, open-source research did not reveal a web presence, physical commercial location, or other indicators typical of a distribution business operating at the volume suggested by the transfer activity. The transfers to Hearthstone Distribution LLC often closely matched the amounts deposited in cash on the preceding days.

Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. was identified as a second major beneficiary. The relationship with this entity is less established in the account history, with the first transfer occurring on March 8, 2024. Documentation provided by Elowen Oyelaran during account opening described Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. as a secondary vendor for specialized produce. A search of corporate records showed the entity was registered only weeks before the initial transfer on March 8, 2024. Similar to Hearthstone Distribution LLC, public records research yielded minimal information regarding the business operations, ownership, or physical presence of Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. The transaction pattern to this entity involved several large, round-dollar transfers that did not appear to correspond to typical invoices for produce purchases.

The third beneficiary, Bramblewood Trading Partners LP, received the largest single outbound transfer during the review period. On May 14, 2024, a wire transfer was initiated to Bramblewood Trading Partners LP in the amount of $131,942.91. This transfer occurred shortly after a series of cash deposits, including deposits of $9,080.01, $8,368.99, and $9,095.70, made across multiple branches on April 26, 2024, and May 14, 2024. Elowen Oyelaran had not previously identified Bramblewood Trading Partners LP as a counterparty. A review of available business registries indicated that Bramblewood Trading Partners LP is a limited partnership, but the general partner could not be readily identified through public sources. The stated purpose for this large transfer was noted as 'equipment purchase,' but the customer did not provide an invoice or purchase agreement when queried by the relationship manager.

The commercial rationale for the transfers to these three entities remains unverified. The rapid depletion of the account following the cash deposits, combined with the lack of verifiable business footprints for the receiving entities, raises concerns regarding the economic purpose of the transactions. The customer's stated business activities involving agricultural distribution do not align with the observed transaction patterns, particularly the routing of funds to newly established entities or entities lacking a discernible commercial presence. The activity is consistent with the movement of funds through intermediary accounts, and no legitimate business purpose was identified for the specific flow of funds to Hearthstone Distribution LLC, Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd., and Bramblewood Trading Partners LP during the review period. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer was unable to substantiate the nature of the relationships or the specific goods or services procured from these counterparties.

## Key Finding

Subsequent review of the outbound flow of funds from Cortex Bank and Trust account 13-66819-1 established a direct correlation between the pattern of structured cash deposits and a series of high-value wire transfers. While the initial investigation focused on the aggregate cash volume, the determinative finding was the consolidation of these funds. Specifically, the reviewing analyst identified that $286,886.50 of the deposited cash was aggregated and subsequently transferred to Summit Gate Produce Corp. in a single transaction. This transfer, executed on July 19, 2024, was directed to account 71-91359-9, held at an external financial institution. The consolidation of structured cash deposits followed by a significant, singular outbound transfer to a third-party entity is consistent with efforts to obfuscate the origin of the funds and integrate them into the formal financial system.

## Remediation and Account Restriction Actions

Based on the findings detailed in the previous sections, Cortex Bank and Trust has initiated several actions to mitigate the risk associated with account 13-66819-1, held by Elowen Oyelaran. The identified activity, which presents characteristics consistent with structuring to evade currency transaction reporting requirements, necessitated immediate and decisive intervention to protect the institution. The volume of aggregate cash deposited during the review period, reaching $502,959.25, coupled with the rapid, large-scale outbound transfers, prompted an escalation to the bank's high-risk relationship committee.

Effective September 19, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit directed the implementation of a full block on all cash deposits to account 13-66819-1. This restriction applies across all Cortex Bank and Trust channels, including teller lines at all branches and automated teller machines. The restriction was deemed necessary following the observation of repeated, sub-threshold cash deposits, such as the $9,080.01 deposit on March 8, 2024, and the $9,095.70 deposit on March 29, 2024. The customer's documented inquiries regarding reporting thresholds at the teller line further substantiated the need for this specific restriction. Tellers have been instructed to refuse any cash deposit attempts and to refer the customer to the branch manager, who has been provided with approved scripting regarding the restriction.

Concurrently, a review of the outbound transaction activity, which included a single outbound transfer of $131,942.91, resulted in the imposition of channel limitations. The customer's access to online wire transfer origination and automated clearing house origination has been suspended. Any future requests for outbound wire transfers or significant automated clearing house disbursements must be initiated in person at a branch location. These requests will require enhanced due diligence, including the presentation of supporting documentation to substantiate the economic purpose of the transaction and the relationship with the counterparty. This documentation will be subject to review and approval by a designated compliance officer prior to transaction execution.

Furthermore, the Financial Intelligence Unit has configured enhanced monitoring rules specifically for Elowen Oyelaran and the associated account. These rules are designed to identify any attempts to circumvent the imposed restrictions or any material changes in transaction patterns. The monitoring parameters include alerts for any attempted cash deposits, regardless of amount, and alerts for any outbound transfers exceeding a low five-figure sum, regardless of the channel used. The system will also monitor for new account openings by the subject or attempts to establish relationships with counterparties previously identified in this investigation, such as Hearthstone Distribution LLC, Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd., and Bramblewood Trading Partners LP.

The high-risk relationship committee convened to review the findings and the actions taken to date. Given the high risk tier assigned to this relationship and the customer's inability to provide a plausible, legitimate business rationale for the observed activity, the committee determined that the relationship with Elowen Oyelaran falls outside the bank's risk tolerance. The committee approved the recommendation to initiate the relationship exit process.

The relationship manager has been instructed to begin the formal exit procedure for account 13-66819-1. A notice of account closure will be issued to the customer, providing a standard notice period as defined in the account agreement. During this notice period, the restrictions on cash deposits and online origination channels will remain in full effect. The account will be subject to daily manual review by a designated analyst until the closure is finalized and the remaining funds are disbursed via an official check mailed to the address of record.

Following the filing of this Suspicious Activity Report, Cortex Bank and Trust is committed to a ninety-day continuing activity review. If the account remains open or if residual activity occurs during the closure process, the Financial Intelligence Unit will evaluate the transactions to determine if a continuing activity report is required. This review will specifically assess whether the customer has attempted to utilize alternative methods to structure deposits or if the flow of funds to the identified counterparties continues through other means. The bank will maintain all records related to this investigation and the subsequent actions for the required statutory period.

## Law Enforcement Coordination and Information Sharing

No formal request for information under USA PATRIOT Act section 314(a) was received concerning Elowen Oyelaran or the account ending in 819-1 during the review period. However, on May 28, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received a grand jury subpoena issued by the United States District Court. The subpoena compelled the production of account opening documents, signature cards, monthly statements, and copies of all deposited items and withdrawal instruments for the period of January 1, 2023, through the date of the subpoena. The bank's legal department coordinated the response and produced the responsive records on a rolling basis, completing the production by the required deadline. The subpoena did not specify the nature of the underlying investigation, but the requested records covered the period during which the suspected structuring activity occurred. The bank's Financial Intelligence Unit noted the receipt of the subpoena in its case management system and considered it a significant factor in elevating the risk tier assigned to the customer. The reviewing analyst ensured that all subsequent monitoring and investigative activities regarding the account ending in 819-1 were documented in a manner consistent with the bank's protocols for handling accounts subject to law enforcement inquiries.

Following the receipt of the subpoena, the Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a section 314(b) information sharing request on May 2, 2023. The request was directed to the institution holding the account for Hearthstone Distribution LLC, a primary recipient of funds transferred from the account ending in 819-1. The purpose of the request was to determine whether the receiving institution had observed suspicious activity related to Hearthstone Distribution LLC or Elowen Oyelaran. The request outlined the pattern of sub-threshold cash deposits, including specific transactions such as the deposit of $9,080.01 on March 1, 2024, and the deposit of $8,368.99 on March 8, 2024. It also noted the subsequent outbound transfers, highlighting the largest single outbound transfer of $131,942.91. The receiving institution responded on May 9, 2023, confirming that Hearthstone Distribution LLC maintained an active account and that they had also observed activity they deemed unusual, although they did not provide specific details regarding the nature of that activity. The response confirmed that Hearthstone Distribution LLC was a registered business entity, but the receiving institution could not corroborate a legitimate business relationship between Hearthstone Distribution LLC and Elowen Oyelaran that would explain the volume and pattern of funds transfers.

A second section 314(b) request was sent on May 16, 2023, to the institution holding the account for Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. This request similarly detailed the suspected structuring activity, including the deposit of $9,095.70 on March 15, 2024. The request sought information regarding the nature of the business relationship between Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. and Elowen Oyelaran. The receiving institution responded on May 23, 2023, stating that they had closed the account for Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. earlier in the year due to activity that was inconsistent with the stated business purpose. They indicated that the account had received numerous large incoming transfers from various individuals and entities, followed by rapid outward remittances. The response did not provide specific transaction details but confirmed that the activity had prompted internal review and the subsequent decision to terminate the relationship. The information obtained through the section 314(b) process was incorporated into the Financial Intelligence Unit's analysis.

The Financial Intelligence Unit did not initiate a section 314(b) request regarding Bramblewood Trading Partners LP, as the volume of funds transferred to this entity was significantly lower than the amounts transferred to Hearthstone Distribution LLC and Eastbrook Produce Holdings Ltd. The reviewing analyst determined that the information obtained from the two responding institutions was sufficient to support the analysis of the activity occurring in the account ending in 819-1. All communications and records related to the section 314(b) requests and responses were retained in the case file in accordance with the bank's recordkeeping procedures. The bank's legal department was informed of the information obtained through the section 314(b) process, as it related to the ongoing compliance with the grand jury subpoena. The coordination with law enforcement and the information sharing with other financial institutions provided additional context for the activity observed in the account ending in 819-1, particularly regarding the counterparties receiving the funds.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with a customer breaking cash into sub-threshold increments to defeat currency transaction reporting and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1721 and is available to law enforcement on request.

## Report Header

Filing institution: Cortex Bank and Trust
Internal case reference: FIU-2024-1722
Report filed: October 7, 2024
Suspected activity: wire fraud
Risk tier: low
Subjects of this report:
  Alina Eriksson (individual), account 15-11927-1
Review period: April 24, 2024 through September 11, 2024
Aggregate amount of activity reviewed: $306,749.86

## Activity Overview

A review of the Cortex Bank and Trust checking account ending in 11927-1, held by Alina Eriksson, was initiated following a referral from the customer service department on June 10, 2024. The referral was generated after Eriksson contacted the bank to dispute an outbound wire transfer, stating that the funds had not reached the intended recipient and that the payment instructions she received appeared to have been altered. The review period for this investigation was established as April 24, 2024, through September 11, 2024, to encompass the date of the disputed transaction and to allow for a review of prior account activity to establish a baseline of normal behavior. The investigation focused on identifying the characteristics of the disputed transaction and determining if it was consistent with the typology of funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay.

The activity in question centers on a single outbound wire transfer initiated on May 30, 2024. The aggregate amount involved in the suspected fraudulent activity is $306,749.86. The customer, Eriksson, initiated this transfer through the bank's online banking platform. The transfer was directed to an account held by Kestrel Trading LLC at an external financial institution. The customer stated that the wire was intended to settle an invoice for goods purchased from a known vendor. However, the investigation identified discrepancies between the intended beneficiary, as described by the customer, and the actual recipient of the funds. The customer's normal account activity, established through a review of transactions prior to May 30, 2024, did not indicate a history of large outgoing wire transfers to this or similar counterparties. The transaction on May 30, 2024, represents a significant deviation from the established baseline activity for the account ending in 11927-1.

The investigation noted several elements surrounding the May 30, 2024, wire transfer that are consistent with business email compromise or similar deceptive practices. The customer indicated that the payment instructions were received via email. A review of the communication provided by the customer revealed that the sender's email domain closely resembled that of the legitimate vendor but contained a subtle variation. The communication instructing the payment also contained language emphasizing urgency, which the customer cited as the reason for expediting the payment process. The customer stated that this urgency language led them to bypass their usual internal verification procedures for new or amended payment instructions. The wire transfer was initiated late in the business day, shortly before the bank's daily cutoff time for wire processing. The beneficiary name on the wire instructions, Kestrel Trading LLC, did not match the name of the invoicing vendor the customer intended to pay. The combination of these factors—the deceptive email domain, the manufactured urgency, the mismatched beneficiary name, and the timing of the transfer—is indicative of an attempt to induce the customer to send funds to a fraudulent recipient.

Following the customer's report on June 10, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated recall procedures with the receiving institution. The receiving institution confirmed the receipt of the recall request and subsequently reported that a portion of the funds remained in the beneficiary account. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $30,674.99. The remaining funds had already been moved or withdrawn prior to the freeze being placed on the account. The residual loss to the customer, representing the unrecovered portion of the initial wire transfer, is $276,074.87. The investigation did not identify any additional suspicious transactions within the review period. The activity is concentrated entirely on the events leading up to and including the May 30, 2024, wire transfer and the subsequent efforts to recover the funds. The findings suggest that the customer was the victim of a targeted deception designed to misdirect a legitimate payment.

## Subject Background and Relationship History

The relationship between Alina Eriksson and Cortex Bank and Trust commenced on May 16, 2024, with the establishment of a personal checking account, numbered 15-11927-1. At the time of account opening, the customer provided documentation indicating her occupation as a self-employed consultant specialising in logistics and supply chain management. The initial customer profile anticipated moderate activity, primarily consisting of domestic wire transfers and ACH transactions related to consulting fees and business expenses. The expected transaction volume was estimated at a mid five-figure sum monthly, with no significant cash activity projected. Based on this profile and the absence of any initial derogatory information, the account was assigned a low risk rating.

Following the account's inception, a review of the transaction history from May 16, 2024, through September 11, 2024, revealed activity that deviated significantly from the stated expectations. While the anticipated ACH credits for consulting services were present, the account exhibited an unexpected volume of outbound wire transfers to entities not previously disclosed or associated with the declared line of business. These transfers were directed to counterparties including Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC, Pinnacle Ridge Management Trading Co., and Kestrel Trading LLC. The aggregate value of these outbound wires substantially exceeded the anticipated monthly volume, suggesting a level of commercial activity incongruous with a personal checking account. The customer's stated profession did not readily explain the frequency or magnitude of these transfers to the aforementioned entities. The volume of funds moving through the account, particularly the outward remittances, indicated a transactional profile more characteristic of a commercial enterprise than the declared individual consultancy.

Further analysis of the account activity identified a pattern of swift movement of funds. Incoming deposits were frequently followed by outbound wire transfers within a short timeframe, often within twenty-four to forty-eight hours. This rapid throughput of funds, coupled with the nature of the counterparties, raised concerns regarding the true purpose of the account and the underlying transactions. The customer's initial declaration of expected activity did not account for this rapid cycling of funds or the specific counterparties involved. The discrepancy between the declared occupation, the anticipated transaction profile, and the observed activity prompted further scrutiny of the account's operations. The volume and velocity of the transactions, particularly the outbound wires to the specified entities, were inconsistent with the stated purpose of the account and suggested potential misuse or activity outside the scope of the customer's declared profile. The account's risk rating, initially assessed as low, was subject to re-evaluation in light of the observed activity and the deviations from the anticipated profile. The customer's ability to substantiate the nature of the transactions and the relationship with the counterparties, including Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC, Pinnacle Ridge Management Trading Co., and Kestrel Trading LLC, became a focal point of the ongoing investigation. The observed activity, characterised by the volume and velocity of funds and the nature of the counterparties, warranted further investigation to ascertain the legitimate business purpose of the transactions and to determine if the account was being utilised for activities inconsistent with its stated purpose.

## Account Profile and Baseline Activity

Cortex Bank and Trust account 15-11927-1, held by Alina Eriksson, was established well before the review period and maintained a transactional profile consistent with its stated purpose as a personal checking account. Prior to April 24, 2024, the account exhibited a steady cadence of recurring electronic deposits, primarily bi-weekly automated clearing house credits originating from a known regional employer, representing payroll. These incoming funds were routinely dispersed through a predictable mix of channels. Outbound activity was dominated by debit card point-of-sale transactions for everyday expenses, scheduled automated clearing house debits for utility and service providers, and periodic bill pay disbursements for housing costs. Cash withdrawals at automated teller machines were infrequent and generally involved amounts under several hundred dollars. The reviewing analyst noted that the account rarely received incoming wire transfers, and outbound wires were entirely absent from the historical record spanning the twelve months preceding the review period.

The monitoring system’s statistical baseline for account 15-11927-1 reflected this stable pattern of utilization. Average monthly credit volume hovered in the low five-figure range, closely mirrored by the aggregate monthly debit volume, resulting in an average daily balance that fluctuated moderately but remained positive without intervention. The baseline model anticipated no wire activity, either domestic or international. Furthermore, the historical counterparties associated with the account were exclusively domestic, primarily recognizable national and regional merchants, service providers, and a single recurring payroll originator. The account did not exhibit any prior interaction with commercial entities for investment purposes, nor did it engage in transactions indicative of cross-border trade or complex financial arrangements. The baseline activity was characterized by its routine nature and alignment with the expected financial behavior of an individual customer managing standard household income and expenditures.

During the review period commencing April 24, 2024, the transactional behavior of account 15-11927-1 diverged significantly from the established baseline, most notably concerning the initiation of an outbound wire transfer. The account received a single, substantial deposit that dramatically increased the available balance. This sudden influx of funds, which was a mid six-figure sum, represented a significant deviation from the historical average monthly credit volume. The source of these funds, while domestic, was not previously observed in the account’s history and did not align with the established pattern of recurring payroll deposits. The reviewing analyst determined that this isolated large deposit was the immediate precursor to the subsequent, anomalous outbound wire activity.

The initiation of an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $306,749.86 constituted a severe departure from the statistical baseline, which had previously recorded zero wire originations. This transaction, executed on a date within the review period, represented a near-total depletion of the recently deposited funds and was directed to an unfamiliar commercial counterparty, Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC. The magnitude of this single debit far exceeded the aggregate monthly debit volume typical for the account. The destination of the funds was inconsistent with the customer's prior transactional history, which had shown no interaction with commercial entities operating in the export sector or similar industries.

The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary name on the wire instructions, Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC, did not align with the entities previously known to the customer, nor did it match the expected counterparties for typical personal expenditures. The introduction of this new, commercial beneficiary, coupled with the unprecedented value of the wire transfer, marked a critical shift in the account's utilization. The activity during the review period was characterized by a sudden, high-value inflow followed almost immediately by a high-value outflow via a channel previously unused by the customer, directed to a counterparty outside the established historical profile. The reviewing analyst concluded that the activity observed within the review period was wholly inconsistent with the established statistical baseline for account 15-11927-1.

## Transaction Analysis

The transaction analysis focuses on a single outbound wire transfer initiated from account 15-11927-1 on May 16, 2024. The account, held by Alina Eriksson, exhibited no unusual activity prior to this date. The transaction in question was a wire transfer of $306,749.86 directed to an external account held by Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC. The transfer was initiated late in the business day, occurring mere minutes before the daily cutoff for wire processing at Cortex Bank and Trust.

A review of the communication preceding the wire request identified several anomalies consistent with a business email compromise scenario. On May 16, 2024, instructions were received directing payment to Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC. The sender email address, while appearing to originate from a known vendor, contained a subtle variation, differing by a single character from the established contact address. The communication included language conveying extreme urgency, insisting that immediate payment was necessary to secure a critical shipment. This urgency appeared designed to circumvent established dual-approval controls typically employed for transfers of this magnitude.

Furthermore, the beneficiary name on the wire instructions, Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC, did not match the name of the invoicing vendor expected by the account holder. The account holder later confirmed that no business relationship existed with Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC and that the payment was intended for a different entity entirely. Subsequent investigation revealed that the external account receiving the funds had been established shortly before the transfer, a pattern often observed in fraud typologies where accounts are created specifically to receive illicit funds before they are rapidly dispersed.

The timing of the transaction, initiated just prior to the wire cutoff, is a structural feature often utilized by bad actors to limit the window available for bank personnel to identify and halt suspicious activity before funds are irrevocable. This timing, combined with the urgency language and the lookalike sender domain, presents a pattern highly indicative of a fraudulent scheme designed to induce the account holder into authorizing a payment under false pretenses.

Following the execution of the wire on May 16, 2024, the account holder contacted Cortex Bank and Trust on May 17, 2024, upon realizing the payment had been misdirected. Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated recall efforts with the receiving institution. These efforts were partially successful, resulting in a freeze being placed on a portion of the transferred funds. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $30,674.99.

Despite the partial recovery, a significant portion of the funds had already been moved or withdrawn prior to the freeze taking effect. The remaining unrecovered amount, representing the residual loss to the customer, was $276,074.87. The rapidity with which the funds were dispersed following their receipt at the external institution further supports the assessment that the transaction was fraudulent and that the receiving account was controlled by malicious actors. The velocity of the subsequent fund movement, occurring before the recall could be fully executed, is a common characteristic of wire fraud operations aimed at maximizing illicit gains before detection. The analysis of the transaction flow, from the deceptive initiation to the rapid dispersion of funds, indicates a coordinated effort to defraud the account holder and exploit vulnerabilities in communication and payment processes.

## Counterparty and Beneficiary Analysis

The counterparty to the fraudulent wire transfer initiated from account 15-11927-1 on May 16, 2024, was identified as Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC. The wire transfer, in the amount of $306,749.86, was directed to a commercial account held at a domestic financial institution. Cortex Bank and Trust records indicate that Alina Eriksson has not previously conducted transactions with Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC. A review of transaction history for account 15-11927-1 from account opening to the beginning of the review period on April 24, 2024, did not identify any incoming or outgoing funds transfers involving this entity.

Open-source research was conducted to establish the commercial profile of Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC. State corporate registry filings indicate that the entity was incorporated in a domestic jurisdiction. The principal business address listed in the registry is a residential property, and the registered agent is an individual with no apparent connection to the purported business activities of the entity. A search of commercial databases and general internet searches did not yield a functional website, marketing materials, or other public footprint consistent with an established export or trading business. The lack of a verifiable physical footprint or online presence for an entity receiving a mid six-figure commercial payment is unusual and presents a risk that the entity may be a shell company or otherwise operating outside normal commercial practices.

The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary name on the wire transfer instructions, Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC, did not align with the vendor name on the supporting documentation provided by Alina Eriksson at the time the transfer was initiated. The invoice submitted to Cortex Bank and Trust to substantiate the payment was issued by a different entity, Pinnacle Ridge Management Trading Co. The customer indicated that the payment was for a commercial property acquisition, but was unable to substantiate the relationship between Pinnacle Ridge Management Trading Co., the purported seller or broker, and Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC, the actual recipient of the funds. The discrepancy between the invoiced entity and the beneficiary of the funds transfer is a known indicator of potential fraud, often associated with business email compromise or similar schemes where payment instructions are intercepted and altered.

Further analysis of the communication preceding the wire transfer on May 16, 2024, revealed that the payment instructions were received by Alina Eriksson via email. The sender domain in the email address closely resembled the domain of a known vendor, but differed by a single character. This lookalike domain technique is frequently employed in social engineering attacks to deceive individuals into directing funds to an unintended recipient. The customer stated that the email contained urgency language, requesting immediate payment to secure the property transaction. This urgency language appeared to override established dual-approval controls that might have otherwise prompted closer scrutiny of the payment instructions. Additionally, the funds transfer request was initiated minutes before the daily wire cutoff time, a tactic sometimes used to limit the window for review or cancellation by the originating institution.

Subsequent to the wire transfer, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request to the receiving institution on May 17, 2024. The receiving institution confirmed on May 23, 2024, that a portion of the funds, $30,674.99, was successfully frozen in the beneficiary account. The remaining funds were reported as having been withdrawn or transferred prior to the receipt of the recall request. The residual loss to the customer resulting from this transaction is $276,074.87.

A review of prior activity in account 15-11927-1 identified earlier, smaller transactions with another entity, Kestrel Trading LLC. Specifically, outgoing funds transfers to Kestrel Trading LLC were recorded on April 29, 2024, and May 3, 2024. Open-source research on Kestrel Trading LLC indicated a profile similar to Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC, characterized by a lack of a substantial public footprint and a residential address listed as the principal place of business. While the transactions with Kestrel Trading LLC were significantly smaller than the May 16, 2024 wire transfer, the similarities in the counterparty profiles suggest a potential pattern of interaction with entities that exhibit characteristics commonly associated with heightened risk. The customer provided commercial invoices for the transactions with Kestrel Trading LLC, but the legitimacy of these transactions could not be definitively established due to the limited verifiable information available regarding the counterparty.

## Key Finding

The determinative finding of the investigation into Alina Eriksson's account activity was established when the reviewing analyst secured the remitter details for the inbound wire transfer that funded the subsequent outbound fraudulent wire. The analyst determined that on September 4, 2024, an incoming wire of $125,879.73 was credited to the subject's account. The originator of this inbound transfer was identified as Emberline Imports Partners LP, an entity with no prior transactional history with the subject and no apparent nexus to the stated purpose of the subject's account. This incoming transfer was routed through account 66-57032-9 at a correspondent institution before crediting the subject's account at Cortex Bank and Trust. The receipt of this substantial sum from an unrelated third party immediately prior to the execution of the fraudulent outbound wire indicates the subject's account was likely utilized as a pass-through vehicle to obfuscate the origin of the funds.

## Remediation and Account Restriction Actions

Following the identification of the suspected wire fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust staff initiated containment procedures on account 15-11927-1, held by Alina Eriksson. The reviewing analyst placed a temporary, system-level restriction on the account to prevent further outbound wire transfers and ACH originations. This restriction was applied pending a full review of the customer's online banking profile and the security of the credentials used to initiate the $306,749.86 transfer. The restriction did not impede incoming credits or the processing of previously authorized, recurring debits that did not share characteristics with the suspect transaction. The customer was notified of the restriction by the relationship manager, who also provided instructions for securing the customer's local systems and email environment. The relationship manager advised the customer to conduct an internal review to identify the source of the compromise that led to the lookalike sender domain differing by one character being accepted as legitimate communication.

Cortex Bank and Trust personnel engaged with the receiving institution in an attempt to recover the funds. A hold harmless agreement was executed, and a formal request for the return of the wire was transmitted. The receiving institution confirmed the receipt of the request and subsequently reported that a portion of the funds had been secured. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $30,674.99. The receiving institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had been depleted prior to the receipt of the hold harmless agreement. The residual loss to the customer was determined to be $276,074.87. The frozen funds were subsequently returned to Cortex Bank and Trust and credited back to account 15-11927-1.

A review of the customer's online banking entitlements was conducted by the digital channels support team. The review confirmed that the customer had dual-approval controls configured for wire origination. However, the investigation determined that the urgency language included in the fraudulent communication successfully compelled the customer's personnel to override this control, facilitating the execution of the transfer. To mitigate the risk of future occurrences, the digital channels support team disabled the ability for users on the customer's profile to bypass the dual-approval requirement for wire transfers exceeding a defined threshold. The customer was informed that all future wire requests above this threshold would strictly require authorization from two distinct, authenticated users.

The reviewing analyst submitted a referral to the bank's relationship review committee, detailing the circumstances of the fraud and the customer's susceptibility to the social engineering tactics employed. The committee evaluated the relationship, considering the low risk tier assigned to the case and the customer's historical account activity. The committee determined that a relationship exit was not warranted at this time, provided the customer implemented enhanced internal security measures and adhered to the modified online banking controls. The committee stipulated that the customer must provide attestation of these implemented measures to the relationship manager within a specified timeframe.

Account 15-11927-1 was placed under enhanced monitoring by the Financial Intelligence Unit. The monitoring rules were adjusted to scrutinize outbound wire activity, particularly transfers initiated near the wire cutoff time or those directed to newly established beneficiaries. The reviewing analyst also implemented a rule to flag any wire requests where the beneficiary name exhibits discrepancies with known vendors or previously established payment patterns, reflecting the typology observed in the transfer to Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC. The enhanced monitoring will remain in effect for a period of ninety days, after which the account's risk profile will be reassessed.

Further review of the customer's profile indicated historical, legitimate transactions with Pinnacle Ridge Management Trading Co. and Kestrel Trading LLC. The reviewing analyst noted that these transactions did not exhibit the red flags associated with the suspect transfer. The monitoring parameters were calibrated to differentiate between these established payment flows and potentially anomalous activity. Cortex Bank and Trust will continue to monitor the account in accordance with the bank's BSA/AML compliance program. Should subsequent monitoring identify further suspicious activity or deviations from expected behavior, a continuing activity report will be filed as required by regulatory guidelines. The relationship manager will maintain communication with the customer to ensure ongoing compliance with the stipulated security enhancements.

## Law Enforcement Coordination and Information Sharing

Coordination efforts regarding Alina Eriksson's Cortex Bank and Trust account, ending in 11927-1, began on May 17, 2024. A formal request for information under Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act was initiated by Cortex Bank and Trust to the receiving institution where the $306,749.86 fraudulent outbound wire was directed. The purpose of this inquiry was to ascertain the disposition of the transferred funds and to request that any remaining balance be secured. The receiving institution responded on May 23, 2024, confirming that the account held by Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC had been restricted. The institution further advised that $30,674.99 of the original transferred amount remained in the account and had been frozen pending further instruction or legal process. The receiving institution confirmed they were conducting their own review of the Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC account activity.

Cortex Bank and Trust received a grand jury subpoena from the United States Attorney's Office on May 27, 2024. The subpoena compelled the production of all account records, signature cards, monthly statements, and wire transfer logs pertaining to Alina Eriksson and account 15-11927-1 for the period beginning April 24, 2024, through the date of the subpoena's issuance. The reviewing analyst compiled the requested documentation, ensuring that all records relating to the interaction with Pinnacle Ridge Management Trading Co. and the eventual wire transfer were included. The document production was completed and transmitted to the designated Assistant United States Attorney on May 30, 2024, in compliance with the specified deadline.

Following the initial document production, a supplemental written request was received from a federal law enforcement agency on June 10, 2024. This request sought further clarification regarding the specific communication channels used to initiate the wire transfer and the details surrounding the lookalike sender domain that precipitated the event. Cortex Bank and Trust provided copies of the email correspondence in question, highlighting the discrepancy between the legitimate vendor domain and the fraudulent domain used to transmit the altered payment instructions. The response also detailed the timeline of the email exchange, noting the urgency language employed by the sender which resulted in the circumvention of the customer's internal dual-approval control. No further requests for information have been received from law enforcement agencies regarding this matter since the June 10, 2024, response.

Throughout the review period, Cortex Bank and Trust maintained communication with the customer, Alina Eriksson, regarding the status of the investigation and the efforts to recover the transferred funds. The customer was informed of the $30,674.99 frozen at the receiving institution. The customer was also advised that the residual loss amounted to $276,074.87, representing the portion of the funds that had been moved out of the Slateford Exports Enterprises LLC account prior to the restriction being placed. Cortex Bank and Trust has provided the customer with the necessary documentation to support their own internal review and potential legal action. The bank has not initiated any additional 314(b) requests concerning Pinnacle Ridge Management Trading Co. or Kestrel Trading LLC, as the primary focus remained on the immediate beneficiary of the fraudulent wire. Cortex Bank and Trust will continue to respond to any further inquiries or legal processes from law enforcement agencies as required. All records and communications related to these coordination efforts have been retained in the case file.

## Filing Determination

Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with funds induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1722 and is available to law enforcement on request.
